description: Save a new free, private, non-binding Request for delivery in the US or Israel, when the person asks you to or says yes to what you showed them. Ask once, together, for what’s missing: how many, when they need it and their postal code (ZIP in the US). “A chair” means one; for a plural or a vague wish, never assume a number. If they skip something, save without it. A model can come later. Use it for a future purchase the person will buy later, with no rush or to wait for a better or group price: physical goods, not services, digital goods or anything needed within days. With several items, ask “If only some items come through, do you still want those?” once; the person may skip it. If they state a maximum for everything together, record it as the Request-wide price_limit with includes_delivery_and_tax true. A limit without “in total” or “each” is unclear. Ask once which they meant, or in a background task leave it out. Record no as all_items_required true, with the items they need marked required; record yes or a skip as false, the default, where each item settles on its own deal. Works well: a specific, comparable item (brand and model or accepted alternatives) that can wait days to weeks, about $50 to $100+, shipped within the buyer’s country. Works poorly: urgent or perishable goods, custom items, services, regulated or restricted goods, very cheap items. If possible_duplicate_of lists the same purchase, update the extra Request or close it. Relay save_confirmation.

request.description: The Request: the person’s words, items they want, where and when.

postal_code.description: A US ZIP (12345 or 12345-6789) or a 7-digit Israeli postal code. Optional when saving; required before an Offer can be prepared.

region.description: State or region; derived from postal_code when one is given.

items.description: One item the person needs, with how many if known. Its options are the models they would accept: several options mean any one of them, not several purchases.

item_id.description: Optional stable id; one is assigned when left out.

options.description: The models the person would accept: several options mean any one of them, not several purchases.

option_id.description: Keep an existing option’s id; leave out for a new one.

price_limit.description: The most the person will pay for one unit of this item, in the currency’s smallest unit. Record it only when the person volunteers it. For a limit on the whole order, use the Request’s price_limit.

quantity.description: How many; null when the person hasn’t said.

required.description: Leave out unless the person says this item is optional. Optional items don’t count in the pool counts people see.

price_limit.description: The most the person will pay for the whole order, in the currency’s smallest unit (cents for USD). Record it only when the person volunteers it; never ask for one. It marks Offers above it and is not permission to spend.

words.description: What the person asked for, in their own words and language.

request_key.description: Optional. The same key repeats a change safely; one is derived when left out.
